# Sveiki | Hello

I am an applied microeconomist with primary research interests in **development economics**, **political economy**, and **economic history**. I study how historical shocks and institutional design shape long-term economic trajectories, with a particular focus on how these effects are distributed unevenly across space. My current work combines geospatial analysis and causal inference to investigate large-scale institutional transitions, exploring how historical disruptions, such as property shocks, interact with local clientelism to create enduring developmental and political lock-ins.

I recently graduated with a Master of Research in Economics from [Sciences Po Paris](https://www.sciencespo.fr/department-economics/en.html), where my research was recognized with the **Best Master Thesis in Economics** award. This followed a B.A. in Economics and Sociology that included an exchange program at [MIT](https://economics.mit.edu/). 

Currently, I am a Trainee in the Data Center of the Prices and Costs Division at the [European Central Bank](https://www.ecb.europa.eu/home/html/index.en.html). Previously, I worked as a Research Assistant in the [Bank of Lithuania](https://www.lb.lt/en/), and held policy and analytical roles at the Lithuanian [Ministry of Environment](https://am.lrv.lt/en/) and [Ministry of National Defence](https://kam.lt/en/).
